Red Hat CSAF 2.0 advisory / VEX fixtures
========================================

Attribution: Red Hat, Inc., Red Hat Product Security. The unmodified JSON files
include the vendor's Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International terms:
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
Original URLs below are the attribution/source links. Detached .asc signatures
and .sha256 companions are retained verbatim alongside each document. These
fixtures were acquired 2026-10-10; vendor generation dates can be newer than the
original advisory publication dates. A pinned historical fixture is not evidence
that a production advisory feed is current.

Production trust roots reside under keys/, not testdata. Detached verification
and signature-time freshness are the signed transport's responsibility; parsing
JSON alone never authenticates the publisher namespace.

Normative semantics consulted
----------------------------
https://redhatproductsecurity.github.io/security-data-guidelines/csaf-vex/
https://redhatproductsecurity.github.io/security-data-guidelines/cpe/
https://redhatproductsecurity.github.io/security-data-guidelines/purl/
https://redhatproductsecurity.github.io/security-data-guidelines/scanning-vendors/
https://access.redhat.com/articles/5554431

Selected product semantics implemented by redhat.go
--------------------------------------------------
* Distro must be native rhel, not Rocky, AlmaLinux, Fedora, or another RPM-
  compatible distribution. Configuration supplies explicit standard/eus/e4s and
  architecture. EUS and E4S require an exact major.minor release.
* A product CPE under vendor Red Hat establishes platform applicability, reached
  through a default_component_of relationship. A package display name or internal
  Errata Tool product ID is not a substitute for that CPE.
* Red Hat explicitly documents RHEL <=9 enterprise_linux major CPEs as spanning
  the lifetime of the mainstream major release. Therefore standard 9.4 and 9.8
  both use the enterprise_linux:9 fixed RPM range. MAIN.EUS is explicitly listed
  among mainstream variants in the CPE guidelines: its .EUS suffix does NOT make
  the RHSA-2024:6783 standard CPE into an EUS-only product. No package release
  suffix such as el9_4 is used to guess a different product servicing stream.
* enterprise_linux with a minor CPE (RHEL 10+) requires the exact configured
  minor. rhel_eus / enterprise_linux_eus and rhel_e4s / enterprise_linux_e4s CPEs
  require the exact selected minor and stream. AUS/TUS, UBI, SAP/layered products,
  JBoss, OpenShift and OCI content are not interpreted as host RHEL applicability.
  Recognized older channel suffixes are baseos, appstream, crb, server,
  workstation, computenode and client; unsupported constraints remain excluded
  under partial coverage, never a clean-product assertion.
* Vendor guidance says xUS scanners must also consult the mainstream unfixed
  CPE. A bare mainstream status cannot by itself prove that an arbitrary xUS
  package remains affected after a backport. Such cross-stream statements are
  retained as AssessmentUnknown, never an unbounded positive or not-affected
  exemption. Only exact selected xUS fixes can reconcile that uncertainty. A
  mainstream fixed EVR is not transplanted into an arbitrary xUS minor.
* Only native pkg:rpm/redhat purls become host package records. Epoch defaults to
  zero when omitted; nonzero epoch, decoded RPM version-release and architecture
  must agree with the vendor's NEVRA name. Binary arch is exact (noarch applies
  across architectures); source purls remain SourcePackage records and are not
  guessed to be installed binaries. Matching a source row requires actual native
  source inventory support in the consumer.
* rpmmod gives name:stream or name:stream:version:context. The normalized key
  retains module name and stream. A declared intermediate module relationship
  is followed with a bounded traversal and checked against the RPM's rpmmod;
  missing host module evidence does not authorize another stream's fix.
* fixed creates a native RPM fixed-version boundary. known_affected without a
  version is unfixed only within its established product; a versioned affected
  purl is an exact affected-version interval. known_not_affected is explicitly
  negative and a versioned negative is limited to that exact EVR.
  under_investigation is AssessmentUnknown, not a positive vulnerability.
* Before publishing, a bare affected/uncertain status for the same CVE, selected
  platform, package, source/binary identity, module and matching architecture is
  reconciled against exact fixes. The earliest fixed EVR is retained rather than
  treating later fixed rebuilds as new vulnerability boundaries. Negative rows
  never erase positive ranges. Combining advisory and VEX archives requires the
  same reconciliation after both documents have been aggregated.
* Unsupported relevant relationship/status constraints fail rather than silently
  expanding applicability. Off-scope product documents are skipped in archives.
  All output remains partial: neither one advisory, legacy VEX nor these weekly
  snapshots prove completeness for unsupported coverage.

Archive boundary
----------------
The caller verifies and stages each original compressed vendor archive before
parsing. parseRedHatArchive streams tar.zst without extracting filesystem paths;
32 MiB per JSON record, 250000 entries, 16 GiB total expanded bytes, 512 MiB zstd
window/memory bound, and 500000 normalized records. Cancellation is checked at
entry boundaries and compressed-reader calls. The archive parser does not renew
freshness; the caller retains verified signature time and artifact provenance.
Observed vendor URLs use advisories/archive_latest.txt and vex/archive_latest.txt
under the CSAF v2 root, pointing to weekly csaf_advisories_YYYY-MM-DD.tar.zst and
csaf_vex_YYYY-MM-DD.tar.zst. Older documents legitimately address products outside
current RHEL: exclusion is not corruption and does not imply a clean inventory.

Tests retain originals unchanged. In-memory derived mutations exercise conflicting
bare/fixed statuses, unsupported relationships, publisher changes and malformed
identity metadata; those mutations are not represented as vendor-authored data.
No checks were executed by the parser implementation worker.
